recount_validated.reasons: Where the truth is known the method is exact, RG's two own records agree with each other, and the independent records agree with the official split on the disputed rows about as often as they agree with the truth on undisputed rows. (1) C1, my own code and links: AO 2025 MatchBeats decrypted with the adapter's decrypt/blocks_of and recounted equals Stage 0 on 731/731 complete player rows for first serves in, 730/731 first-serve points won, 731/731 second-serve points won. (2) C2: my own MatchBeats recount (RG 2022-2025) and Olympic play-by-play recount agree with the official split on all 1,688 proposed sides they hold completely; 0 contradict (18 incomplete, 12 absent). This is not independent (same venue systems), so it is used only as a veto. (3) C3, my own parse of the raw API files and my own links by round and names: RG's statistics equal Sackmann's raw rows on all eight counts for 2,732 of 2,740 player rows of 2019-2021 (the 8 are 2021 rows); the winner flag agrees on 2,740/2,740; the lead's official values equal my raw parse on all 6,574 RG player rows I re-parsed (the other 6 of 6,580: four Soboleva/Sobolieva rows my name test cannot pair, checked by their opponents in official_raw.py, and the one unplaced match). (4) Independent referees: MCP and Court Vision 2022 side with the official split (see the classes).

RGFSA.reasons: Independent records, judged against their own error where the truth is not disputed. MCP is calibrated on 172 RG 2019-2021 player rows where RG = Sackmann: first serves in exact 72.7% (78.1% where serve points match). On all 158 proposed sides with a chart, MCP equals the official count 127 times and Sackmann's 18 times (H_O, official right, predicts 114.8 and 14.6; H_S, Sackmann right, predicts 11.1 and 114.8). Whole-split test (points moved among first/second won/lost): RG 138 rows, official closer 132, Sackmann closer 4, tie 2, log10 LR +512. By sign: + 108-3, - 17-1, 0 5-0. By size: |d|<=1 65-3, >=2 65-1. Court Vision is reliable for RG 2019, 2020 and 2022 (92.5-100% exact on undisputed rows; one faulted-first-serve row per second-serve point) but not for 2023-24 (21-66%). On 232 complete RG 2022 proposed rows it sides with the official record 230-1 (1 tie, log10 LR +1028), signs + 191-0, - 16-1, 0 6-0. The '-' sides are the same fault, but only away from both-minus matches: there the referees side with RG 29-0. On both-minus matches they split 4 for RG, 3 for Sackmann, 1 tie, and on Van de Zandschulp MCP and CV disagree with each other. The official record may be the one off there (missed first-serve faults for both players mirror Sackmann's fault), so those rows are not corrupt beyond reasonable doubt. Pooled rates: Sackmann's first serves in jump in 2022-2025 (men's qualifying 68.5/65.3/65.2/68.6% against 61.3-62.7% in 2019-2021; women's qualifying 69.9/68.1/67.1/68.6% against 64.2-65.2%). The same Sackmann files show no such jump at the clay Masters (men's qualifying 61.2-63.7% in 2019-2025), the AO or Wimbledon. After the fix: men's qualifying 63.2/62.2/61.5/63.5%, women's 65.5/65.2/64.1/64.1%, main draws 61.5-63.7%. Double faults per second-serve point fall to the official record's level (men's qualifying 2022: 11.7 to 10.1%, official 10.1%; women's qualifying 2025: 14.7 to 12.9%, official 13.2%). Within each edition, the rows where the two records agree read 62.6-65.4% first serves in; the disputed rows read 61.6-63.8% by RG and 65.5-70.0% by Sackmann. Values and links: all proposed values equal RG's raw API documents. Serve points and serve points won are equal. Round, winner and score agree (5 retirements where RG adds a 0-0 set). Names match or are legitimate variants (Kuzmova/Hruncakova, Paar/Andrei, Soboleva/Sobolieva). X3: Stage 0 drops Pigossi-Kawa for B3, caused by this very fault (Pigossi 55 first serves in of 58). The fix would make the match pass every check and bring it back with Kawa's side still corrupt and unproposed (class points: 36 first serves in where RG has 23, serve points 51 against 48). A corrupt box is worse than none, so the side stays as it is.

RGFSB.reasons: The split of B rows is the same fault and the official split is right. Court Vision 2022 sides with RG on 17-0 complete B rows, MCP on 2-0, and the second record agrees on 275 of 282 sides (0 contradict). Correcting the split alone is a clear, unique operation. It writes exactly the official three counts, guarded by Sackmann's own serve points, aces and double faults, and keeps serve points won. B6 and B7 pass after the fix. The Stage 0 rates that use aces and double faults (per serve point) do not change, while first serves in, first-serve won and second-serve won become right, so no rate gets worse. Caveat: the differing counts are Sackmann's errors too. Where an independent record holds them, it equals the official value every time (MCP aces 3/3, double faults 5/5; CV 2022 aces 5/5, double faults 15/15; never Sackmann's). Sackmann's double faults are mostly one short, consistent with a missed double fault booked as a first serve in and lost. These counts remain wrong after the fix; that would be a separate correction, not proposed.

OGFSA.reasons: No clean Olympic edition shows that the Olympic results file measures what Sackmann measures, and MCP is noisier at the Olympics (exact first serves in on 59.5% of undisputed Olympic rows against 78% at RG). The Olympic record is right where the disagreement is Sackmann's established fault. MCP's whole-split test favours it on 10 of 10 '+' sides (OGFSA and OGFSB) and on the 1 '0' side charted (log10 LR +42 to +53 over the Olympic charts). Within the event, the undisputed rows read 65.5% (men) and 64.0% (women) first serves in; the disputed rows read 63.7/61.6% by the Olympic file and 75.9/73.4% by Sackmann. The '-' sides are not corrupt beyond reasonable doubt. Of the only two charted, one equals Sackmann's split exactly (Fernandez) and one is between the records (Muchova); both are in first-round matches where both players read 1-2 fewer from Sackmann (the pattern under which RG's record was also doubtful); and the Olympic record contradicts itself in one '-' side's match (Gauff-Carle: play-by-play 8 second-serve points won for Carle, statistics 7). The '-' differences are 1-2 points, so leaving them costs little. Values: all equal the raw Olympic JSON (status OFFICIAL, PTS_WON_SERVE = first + second won, 2ND_SERVE attempts = serve points - first serves in); the Olympic play-by-play recount agrees on every complete side.

other_findings: 1. The only row Stage 0 now drops that the fix would bring back is Pigossi-Kawa, and its other side stays corrupt (X3). The other 13 dropped RG/Olympic rows stay dropped. They are classes points/other, rightly not proposed. Four of them fail B3/B6 from the fault's extreme form, where every serve point is booked as a first serve in (Barrios Vera-Kovalik 25/25 and 19/19, Uchijima-Yuan 28/28 and 23/23). A future fix of those would need serve points too. 2. In 69 in-scope matches the other side is class points (serve points or serve points won differ; 40 with first serves in off by 3 or more) and stays as it is. These matches already pass Stage 0's checks today; the fix improves one side. 3. Court Vision: the RG 2023-24 copy is unreliable for this purpose (exact first serves in on 21-66% of undisputed rows). Its faulted-first-serve rows cover only 0.74 and 0.46-0.48 of second-serve points. By serve_num its second-serve share falls only to 36.5% and 35% (the lead's 27%/16% are shares with a fault row). The 2021 men's copy is partly incomplete (73%). 4. SofaScore equals Sackmann on all four split counts for 99.5% of 1,508 linked RG 2022-25 main-draw player rows, including 100% of the 111 class-points rows. It shares Sackmann's record (C5 confirmed) and is no referee. 5. The lead's link.mcp_rows sets draw to 'qual' for every round starting with 'Q', so all 64 quarter-final player rows (RG 2019-25, Olympics) are unlinked and absent from agree_mcp_*.csv. My link reproduces the lead's other 704 rows exactly. No effect on the proposal. 6. X1 was found by looking where the contrary verdicts fall, so it is post hoc. It only removes corrections (conservative), and a mechanism fits it (missed first-serve faults in the official record for both players of a match). The 13 RG both-minus matches are all on outside courts (12, 8, 14, 9, 13, 2, 11), with no strong single-court cluster; the 3 Olympic ones are first-round women's matches. 7. Two in-scope B sides (Gauff and Kanepi, RG 2022) have Sackmann's double faults blank. Stage 0 keeps those matches as partial (dropped); the fix is harmless there. 8. The Olympic results file and its play-by-play disagree on one side (Carle vs Gauff, R32), which the lead's veto removed. 9.
